characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system attached to field emission gun SEM (FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 35%Mn steel only a single austenite phase is present (no ferrite; ferrite listed as '-' in Table 3), with average grain size D_FCC-G/T of 33 ± 1.6 μm and twin boundary fraction f_Tw of 59.6% (about 60%).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground and electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; grain size by linear intercept with boundary misorientation angle definition of 15°, using Channel 5 software
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase distribution and grain size as a function of alloying content; measure austenite grain size and twin boundary fraction

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbides are uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix; the average κ-carbide size for 35%Mn is about 2 nm (Table 3: 2.0 ± 1.1 nm) — the finest of the Mn series; SAED shows the coherent γ/κ orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operated at 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at 20 V and −20 °C; dark-field images taken along the [001]γ zone axis using a κ-carbide diffraction spot
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the variation in κ-carbide size and distribution with alloying content
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dark-field imaging with SAED

characterization_methods.key_findings: Density of the Mn-35 steel is 6.53 g/cm3 (Table 1).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure experimental density of the steels as a function of alloying content

characterization_methods.key_findings: Mn-35: YS 401 MPa, UTS 849 MPa, UE 60%, A 75.0%; σ_TS 1313 MPa and σ_FS 2200 MPa; maximum work hardening rate ~2300 MPa.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Initial strain rate 1.1 × 10^-3 s^-1 at ambient temperature; gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm specimens cut with tensile axis parallel to rod axis; average of two specimens
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure room-temperature stress-strain response, yield strength, tensile strength, elongation and strain hardening rate after solution treatment

characterization_methods.key_findings: Mn-35 Charpy impact energy Akv at −40 °C = 19.3 ± 2.1 J.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Tested at −40 °C; specimens cut from solution-treated rods with the V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis; average of two specimens
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure impact toughness of the solution-treated low-density steels

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 59.6% (about 60%) for the 35%Mn steel.

interfaces.interface_notes: The κ-carbides assume a coherent interface with the austenite matrix as evidenced by SAED observations; strengthening therefore follows a particle shear model rather than Orowan.
interfaces.phase_evolution: No ferrite present at 35%Mn; only a single austenite phase after solution treatment. κ-carbide precipitation originates from spinodal decomposition and ordering of C and Al in the austenite; κ-carbide size decreases with increasing Mn content (5 nm at 25%Mn to 2 nm at 35%Mn).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Within the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series after 1050 °C/2 h + WQ, increasing Mn content from 20% to 35% decreases yield strength from 896 MPa to 401 MPa while total elongation increases from 28.5% to 60% and the work hardening rate increases; the Mn-35 grade (YS 401 MPa, UTS 849 MPa) is the softest grade studied and higher Mn content improves impact toughness relative to lower-Mn high-C/high-Al grades.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Each steel composition was melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace with a 50 kg capacity, then cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm. Applies to all designed compositions including the Fe(x)Mn11Al1C series (Mn-35).
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, then air-cooled to room temperature (this is the parent hot-rolled process proc_hot-rolled).

Hot-rolled rods solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this is the main終態 (state_label 1050 °C–2 h–WQ) used for tensile tests, Charpy impact toughness and EBSD/TEM characterization.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Two solution-treated specimens tested; data reported as average value of two specimens; MTS tensile machine and MTS impact tester (500 J capacity)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Tensile specimens with gauge length 25 mm and diameter 5 mm cut with tensile axis parallel to rod axis; Charpy specimens with V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis

fracture_toughness.value: 19.3 ± 2.1 J (Charpy V-notch impact energy Akv at −40 °C)

strain_hardening_rate.note: maximum work hardening rate, obtained in the 35%Mn steel

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with abundant Σ3 twin boundaries

precipitates.coherency: coherent with the austenite matrix (orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ)
precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching the Mn-35 steel (Fe34.23Mn11.10Al1.00C) consists of a single austenite (FCC) phase — no ferrite — with a coarse austenite grain size of about 33 μm, a twin boundary fraction of about 60% and uniformly distributed nano-scale κ-carbides of about 2 nm.

unmapped_findings: For the Mn-35 sample the maximum true stress just before necking σ_TS (UTS^a) is 1313 MPa and the fracture strength σ_FS (FRS^a) is 2200 MPa (Table 2); text states σ_TS ≈ 1350 MPa and σ_FS ≈ 2150 MPa are nearly constant for all investigated compositions and do not vary significantly with C, Mn and Al content.
Nominal/measured chemical composition of the Mn-35 steel (Table 1): C 1.00, Mn 34.23, Al 11.10, Fe Bal., density 6.53 g/cm3.
The Mn-35 steel shows the largest austenite grain size (~33 μm) and the softest grade (YS ~401 MPa) among the investigated compositions.
The κ-carbide size decreases with increasing Mn content: 5 nm at 25%Mn to 2 nm at 35%Mn; the 35%Mn sample shows the finest and most sparsely resolved κ-carbide particles of the Mn series.

Except for the 0.6%C and 30%Mn steels, the work hardening rate vs true strain of the other steels (including 35%Mn) shows a typical behaviour: a rapid decline followed by a slow rise and then another decline (the 0.6%C and 30%Mn steels show a monotonic decrease).
